data.content_ref: inline:The claim identifies sky-view factor as the single cross-city modulator, but the mechanism text undercuts that singularity by making the urban fabric's higher thermal mass/heat capacity versus the countryside the precondition for the stored-heat asymmetry. If the stored-heat asymmetry is a necessary precondition, then a low-sky-view city built on low-thermal-mass materials (e.g., timber/light-frame construction) would not produce a larger nocturnal gap than a high-sky-view city built on high-thermal-mass masonry, so cross-city variation cannot be governed by sky view alone. The target thus fails to justify a 'single mechanism' for the cross-city gap while its own countercondition (comparable/higher rural thermal mass) shows storage mass can dominate or erase the effect.
